title: Beyond Small Talk: Modeling Disclosure Trajectories in Human-AI Conversation
abstract: arXiv:2610.29413v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recently, we see a rise in conversational agents as a form of social and emotional support, where disclosure will unfold over time. Yet, current evaluations of these agents typically examine isolated conversational states. In analyses of naturally occurring conversations, disclosure history and current disclosure are confounded which tends to make their effects difficult to isolate. We thus introduce Trajectory-based Disclosure Evaluation (TraDE), an evaluation framework grounded in Social Penetration Theory that utilizes predefined disclosure trajectories and evaluates how preceding disclosure history shapes model behavior under matched current disclosure. Through the use of TraDE, we demonstrate across multiple models and relational behavior benchmarks that responses to disclosures matched on depth can differ depending on the preceding trajectory, particularly in whether models accept or challenge the user's framing. translated_title: 超越闲聊：人机对话中的自我披露轨迹建模
translated_abstract: 近年来，对话式代理作为一种提供社会性和情感支持的方式日益兴起，其中自我披露会随时间逐步展开。然而，目前对这些代理的评估通常只考察孤立的对话状态。在对自然发生的对话进行分析时，披露历史与当前披露相互混淆，导致二者的效应难以被分离。为此，我们提出了基于轨迹的披露评估框架TraDE，该框架以社会渗透理论为基础，利用预定义的披露轨迹，评估在当前披露水平相同的条件下，先前的披露历史如何塑造模型的行为。通过使用TraDE，我们在多个模型和关系行为基准上证明：即使披露深度相互匹配，模型对披露的回应仍可能因先前的轨迹不同而有所差异，尤其体现在模型是接受还是挑战用户的表述框架上。我们还观察到（摘要在此处截断）……
tldr: 本文提出基于社会渗透理论的TraDE评估框架，通过预定义披露轨迹来评估在当前披露相同的条件下，先前的披露历史如何影响人机对话中模型对用户自我披露的回应方式。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces TraDE, a Social Penetration Theory-grounded evaluation framework that uses predefined disclosure trajectories to assess how preceding disclosure history shapes model responses to user disclosure in human-AI conversations under matched current disclosure levels.
